struck: Houses averaged 122 days to sell in 2026.
use: Houses averaged 122 days from listing to an accepted offer from January to September 2026.

struck: On the middle house of the year ($362,000), the 2.7 percent between the last list price and the sale is about $9,800. On the middle condo ($232,000), the 4.0 percent is about $9,300.
use: A house that sold for $362,000 at 97.3 percent of its last list price had been listed at about $372,000, about $10,000 more.

struck: Condos went from 117 days (August) to 142 (October).
use: Condos went from 117 days in August 2026 to 142 in October 2025.

struck: Spring listings sell faster and closer to ask.
use: In 2026 more buyers signed in spring, but days to an accepted offer moved little from month to month.

pattern: \bmost common (?:sale|home sold)\b[^.]{0,80}\b(?:on|in) the Grand Strand\b|\bmost common sale\b[^.]{0,40}\bacross\b
struck: The Myrtle Beach condo is the most common sale across CCAR's areas.
use: In the Myrtle Beach area, condos outnumbered houses, 1,252 sales to 480.

struck: About 1 in 9 resales in Horry County went to a company rather than a person: 613 of 6,866 houses and 671 of 4,181 condos.
use: About 1 in 9 resales in Horry County went to a company rather than a person: about 1 in 12 houses and other homes, and about 1 in 6 condos.

struck: About 1 in 9 resales went to companies, most of them investors.
use: (say 'a company'; the deeds do not show what each company is for)

pattern: \b93 percent of the county'?s?\b|\babout 93 percent\b|\b71 percent of (?:it|the county)
struck: Companies paid a median of about 93 percent of the county's value for the resale houses they bought.
use: Companies paid a median of about 94 percent of the county's value for the houses they bought from owners. People paid about 101 percent.

struck: The company paid a median of about $172,000 and sold for about $258,000, about 45 percent more.
use: Half of these houses resold for about 45 percent or more above what the company paid.

struck: A cash buyer closed 13 days after the listing date.
use: A cash buyer closed within 13 days of the day he listed.

struck: Listed in that condition, houses here sold for 97.3 percent of their last list price.
use: Houses sold through the MLS went for 97.3 percent of their last list price on average this year.

struck: On the middle Horry County home, about $350,000, the costs the law sets come to $1,320 with a mortgage to release.
use: On the middle $350,000 home with a mortgage to release, the fees in state law that the state contract puts on the seller come to $1,320.

struck: Agents' fees are negotiable and not set by law.
use: Agents' fees are fully negotiable, and no law fixes them.

struck: When the seller's permanent home is outside South Carolina, the buyer must hold back part of the price for state income tax: 5.21 percent for a 2026 sale.
use: When the seller's permanent home is outside South Carolina, the buyer must hold back 5.21 percent for state income tax on a 2026 sale, unless the gain on a main home is inside the federal exclusion.

struck: If you sell as is, you can skip the disclosure form.
use: Selling as is does not by itself remove the state's disclosure form.

struck: A cash contract has no financing box to fail.
use: A cash offer does not depend on the buyer getting a loan.

struck: Wholesaling is illegal in South Carolina.
use: South Carolina law bars a brokerage from wholesaling.

struck: 4.5 mo; 103 days; +10.5 % Median Price YoY; 4.3 months of supply; condo inventory is at about 7.6 months
use: Months of supply, September 2026: 4.2 for houses, 7.5 for condos.

struck: Homes not priced and marketed correctly average about 121 days on market. Well-priced homes still sell in 30-60 days.
use: Houses averaged 122 days from listing to an accepted offer from January to September 2026.

struck: Zillow and Redfin AVMs are routinely off by 10 to 25%.
